Grade 8 Science: Friction and Sound
Friction is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact. Rough surfaces usually produce more friction than smooth surfaces. Oil and grease reduce friction between moving machine parts. Grooves on shoe soles and tyre treads improve grip.
Sound is produced by vibrating objects. Sound needs a medium such as air, water or solids to travel. It cannot travel through a vacuum. Faster vibrations produce a higher pitch. Larger vibrations produce a louder sound. A vibrating ruler makes sound when it moves the surrounding air. These notes cover only friction and sound for Grade 8. Review both topics closely.
